successCriteria.description: `npm run build` in web/ (tsc --noEmit + vite build) completes with zero TypeScript errors and emits a production bundle.
A component test asserts the login success flow routes to the dashboard AND persists the returned token in sessionStorage (not merely that login was invoked).
A component test asserts the login failure flow renders the server's error message verbatim and adds no email-existence hint (no distinct message for unknown vs wrong-password email).

A component test asserts the 401-redirect behaviour: an authenticated call (e.g. getMe) returning 401 clears the token from sessionStorage and routes to /login rather than rendering an empty/blank page.
A test asserts the bearer token is attached as `Authorization: Bearer <token>` on authenticated API calls (and absent on the public login call).
web/README.md documents `npm install`, `npm run dev` (Vite proxy → local Fastify API), `npm run build`, and `npm test`, plus the sessionStorage token behaviour and the 401-redirect flow.
No file under src/ is modified; the existing backend build and its 181 tests remain green.

constraints: Tests use Vitest + Testing Library (jsdom), placed under web/src/**/*.test.tsx alongside the modules they cover; no new test framework or runner is introduced.
No production source under src/ is modified — this phase is confined to web/ (tests + README).

Tests reference the existing public entry points (web/src/presentation/index.ts, web/src/modules/auth/index.ts, web/src/infrastructure/api/index.ts, web/src/shared/date/index.ts) and the canonical shared types — they must not re-declare or diverge from those contracts.
The 401-redirect test must exercise the single code path (RequireAuth via useAuth) — it must not introduce a second redirect mechanism.
The login-failure test must assert the message is the server's verbatim error and that no email-existence distinction is introduced (enumeration-safe).
outOfScope: Any change to backend source under src/ (build, tests, routes, services, repositories) — the 181 backend tests must remain untouched.
New frontend features or production code changes — this phase only adds tests and documentation; existing web/ production modules are treated as fixed contracts.
E2E/browser tests and smoke-script changes — coverage is component/unit level via Vitest + Testing Library.

ambiguities.description: How the 401-redirect component test should simulate the authenticated-call-returns-401 scenario (the existing RequireAuth.test.tsx only covers no-token and token-restore, not a 401-clearing path).
options: Drive it through AuthProvider with a getMe fake that rejects ApiError(401) and assert the guard redirects to /login
Assert at the ApiClient level (token cleared) plus a separate guard test for session===null redirect, treating them as two halves of one behaviour
Add a dedicated integration test wiring ApiClient+AuthProvider+RequireAuth together

ambiguities.description: Whether the login-success test must assert the token is actually written to sessionStorage (the existing LoginPage.test.tsx asserts navigation and login invocation but not token persistence).
options: Assert tokenStorage.setToken was called with the returned token
Assert sessionStorage.getItem contains the token via a real TokenStorage
Treat AuthService.login's setToken as already covered by auth.service.test.ts and only assert navigation

entityInvariants.invariant: A session is either null (anonymous) or carries { token, profile, status: AUTHENTICATED }; the token is the single source of truth persisted in sessionStorage, and the in-memory profile is re-fetched via getMe on restore.
The token lives only in sessionStorage (cleared on tab close, survives reload); it is cleared on logout and on any authenticated 401, and never decoded client-side for expiry.

interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: On failure, propagate the server's error message verbatim with no email-existence distinction; a failed login must not clear an already-stored token.
A 401 clears the stored token and surfaces ApiError(status 401) so callers route to login.
Clears the token and returns to anonymous state; safe to call when already logged out.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: Tests must import the canonical shared types (EmployeeProfile, LoginResponse, LeaveRequestView, LeaveBalanceView, AuthSessionStatus, EmployeeRole, EmploymentStatus) from the shared-types entry point rather than re-declaring them.

Tests must use the public auth entry point (AuthProvider, useAuth, IAuthService, AuthSession) and the public API entry point (IApiClient, ITokenStorage, ApiError, TokenStorage) — never module internals.
The 401-redirect test must match the single redirect code path implemented by RequireAuth (session === null → Navigate to /login, holding while isRestoring).
The bearer-token test must match the ApiClient contract: Authorization header only on authenticated requests when a token is present, and token cleared on authenticated 401.
README must reflect the actual Vite proxy targets (localhost:3000 for /auth, /employees, /leaves, /balances) and the actual npm scripts (dev/build/test).

integrationPoints.why: Component tests render pages/guards inside AuthProvider with injected IAuthService/ITokenStorage/IApiClient fakes to drive login, restore, and 401-redirect flows.
Bearer-header and 401-clearing behaviour is asserted against the real ApiClient with a mocked global fetch and real TokenStorage/sessionStorage.
The 401-redirect test asserts the guard routes to /login (not an empty page) when the session is anonymous after a 401 clears the token.
